title: Promoter result 1.0
description: Structural public result contract; synthetic validation is not prediction or scientific validation. See ../docs/validation/promoter-runtime.md.
$comment: Validate strict JSON first: reject duplicate keys and NaN/Infinity. Schema acceptance proves neither equations, term sums, score/log relations, hashes or stable IDs, coordinate transforms/bounds/nonempty intervals, deadlines, request/output resolution, eligible-state counts, tie selection nor array ordering. Runtime/adapters must check all these, coverage/status-count sums and denominators, complete_context, every requested candidate and complete state in order, one selected marker, IDs matching their parent coordinates and receipt, required warnings, host NFC, metadata canonical bytes/depth and all effective record/batch/all-state budgets. Resolved integer coordinates/counts and float settings must have the prescribed serialized numeric representation; JSON Schema treats integral floats as integers and integers as numbers. Hashes use compact sorted-key ensure_ascii=True allow_nan=False JSON, no newline. Authoritative result bytes use json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, indent=2, ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False) plus exactly one LF, default indent separators, UTF-8 without BOM. Check both received uncompressed bytes and authoritative reserialization bytes <= max_result_json_bytes before accepting; this schema cannot measure either or enforce serialization. Empty valid supported scans preflight to no_candidate/empty_scan with complete zero coverage regardless of expired deadlines; rejected scans retain invalid_input/unsupported precedence. Full semantic validation and real-runtime/source parity remain required.

coordinate.$comment: Resolved coordinates must serialize as JSON integers. JSON Schema integer also accepts integral floats; parser/runtime must enforce normalized representation, ascending nonempty intervals, lengths and bounds.

finite.$comment: Finite binary64 bounds reject infinities. NaN is not a JSON number; reject nonfinite tokens in the parser, before validation.

limits.$comment: Exactly the 20 effective limits, each positive and at most its published ceiling. Lower values are allowed. The four default/max deadline values must serialize as floats; JSON Schema cannot distinguish 30 from 30.0. Runtime checks defaults <= maxima and all effective cross-field budgets.

diagnostic.$comment: Error code/field/message are required. Located normalization and limit diagnostics may add index, character, limit or observed data; their exact extra key set is not fixed by the public contract.

warning.$comment: Warning payload interiors are not fixed; code is required. Runtime verifies required host/legacy warning codes and explanatory text.

range.$comment: [a,b) may be empty; runtime checks a <= b <= normalized sequence length and (b-a)*strand_count against the planned-site budget.

selected_state.$comment: Elements are optional only on the separate selected state copy. Listed states require a selected boolean, never elements. Genomic intervals appear iff projection is present; enforced at record scope. Equations, interval arithmetic, IDs, score bounds versus log and state visit/selection order require semantic validation.

listed_state.$comment: Elements are optional only on the separate selected state copy. Listed states require a selected boolean, never elements. Genomic intervals appear iff projection is present; enforced at record scope. Equations, interval arithmetic, IDs, score bounds versus log and state visit/selection order require semantic validation.

record.$comment: Rejected fields echo null unless independently validated. Normalization information survives later rejection. Metadata is arbitrary parsed JSON, not controls; canonical bytes/depth and the validation history are runtime checks. Output options are not emitted: states/legacy/elements presence must be compared with the resolved request. Projection presence is enforced for every scored state here.

model.$comment: The 12 model keys are fixed. source and parameters interiors intentionally remain extensible typed JSON objects; only parameters.parameter_json_sha256 has an agreed required nested name. No candidate identity is invented. Verify source pins, array hashes/counts/unused indices, utility tables, exact term_source_names/terms_semantics and static source_quirks against the installed model and receipt. This structural schema does not certify their scientific content.

batch.$comment: Public synthetic adapter uses sparse status_counts; known status keys only, zero-valued entries may be present. Runtime verifies counts against results, actual deadlines <= effective maxima, and complete iff no failed record. Deadline values must serialize as floats, which JSON Schema cannot distinguish from integers.
